card: Unifies peer send pause tracking by replacing a separate boolean flag and start timestamp with a single atomic timestamp where epoch represents the unpaused state. This eliminates duplicate synchronization logic in message sending and queuing and allows peer inactivity checks to read the pause status and duration atomically. It is an internal refactor following up on merged PR #36667.
changed_since_previous: None; the patch and commit set match the earlier description.
evidence: Follow-up to merged PR #36667 ("net: enforce timeout interval for paused send peers").
Removes redundant state update code across CConnman::SocketSendData and CConnman::PushMessage in src/net.cpp.
problem: A peer's send pause state was tracked across two separate variables: a boolean flag and a start timestamp. Updating and synchronizing them was duplicated across message queueing and socket send paths, and the peer inactivity check read both variables separately rather than as a single atomic snapshot.

risk.why: A logic error in send pause tracking or inactivity checks could stall message processing or trigger premature peer disconnects.

summary: Consolidates peer send pause tracking in CNode by removing the separate boolean flag and representing the paused state entirely through an atomic timestamp, where epoch represents unpaused. Access and state updates are centralized into CNode methods, and test-only pause resets are moved into ProcessMessagesOnce.
